# Segmental Spine Kinematics and Loads

## Status

Evidence class: implemented software pathway, scientifically unqualified;
chapter text approved by the owner on 2026-10-15 after the Astra, Argon and
Fable panel review; no result approved. This chapter is the calculation-level reference for the
segmental-spine pathway of epic #12735 (children SPN-0 to SPN-17,
consolidated by #12773). No calculation is registered. The registry blocker
`UP-D1-segmental-spine-inventory` stays open until UP-D1 inventories the

- A successful render of this chapter is not approval.

The binding conventions are ADR-0055

## Scope, Units and Module Paths

No repository-generated number in this chapter describes an individual golfer
or comes from a licensed SimTK model. Fixture numbers are invented and are
labelled so. Literature numbers describe their published cohorts and carry
their recorded `verified_from_primary` status.

Units:

- Segmental, coupling and distribution angles are radians.
- Golf-term angle outputs are degrees. Legacy golf-term inputs whose names end
  in `_rad` are radians.
- Forces are N, moments N·m, lengths m, time s. Body-weight normalisation uses
  $g = 9.80665$ m/s² and gives BW and BW·m.

Two packages share the name `spine`. This chapter always gives the full path:

| Short Name | Path | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Shared `spine` | `src/shared/python/spine/` | Engine-independent levels, composition, coupling laws, distribution, golf terms, load contract, context bands, movement variants, visualization data and plots |
| OpenSim `spine` | `src/engines/physics_engines/opensim/python/spine/` | Fixture, inventory, coupler extraction, golf input, drive, motion reader, inverse dynamics, static optimization, joint reactions, studies, aggregation and sensitivity |
| Static-optimization core | `src/engines/physics_engines/opensim/python/static_opt_core.py` | Numeric core shared with the leg static optimization |
| Load providers | `src/shared/python/injury/spinal_load_providers.py` | Heuristic and model spinal-load providers |

## Conventions and Frames

Frames:

- Every vertebra, the sacrum, the pelvis and the named terminal body carry an
  ISB-style frame: X anterior, Y cranial, Z right.
- These are the repository's ADR-0055 conventions, implemented as profile
  `isb_spine` of `biomechanics/joint_conventions.py`. Direct comparison with
  Wu et al. (2002) is pending: the primary text was not read
  (`verified_from_primary: false`, #12737).

Level transform:

- A level $i$ joins an inferior (caudal) and a superior (cranial) vertebra.
  Its transform maps the superior frame into the inferior frame:
  $$T_i = T_{i,0}\, T\!\left(R_{ZXY}(\theta_i),\, d_i\right), \qquad
  R_{ZXY}(\theta) = R_z(\theta_{FE})\,R_x(\theta_{LB})\,R_y(\theta_{AR}).$$
- $T_{i,0}$ is the neutral offset (lordosis or kyphosis), read natively from
  the model's offset frames. Its rotation block is $N_i$. It is excluded from
  reported angles and included in every composition.
- $d_i$ is the joint translation. It is zero for rotational models.
- $\theta_{FE}$ is about Z, $\theta_{LB}$ about the floating X axis and
  $\theta_{AR}$ about Y.

Signs:

- $\theta_{FE} > 0$ is extension.
- $\theta_{LB} > 0$ is right lateral bending.
- $\theta_{AR} > 0$ is left axial rotation.
- The decomposition is singular at $|\theta_{LB}| = 90°$ (gimbal lock). The
  shared extractor flags it through `OrientationResult.singular`.

Levels:

- The 17 thoracolumbar disc levels L5-S1 to T1-T2 are defined by
  `SpinalLevel` in the shared `spine` package. They are ordered caudal to
  cranial and are contiguous.
- Cervical levels are out of scope.

Lab quantities take explicit `up` and `target` unit vectors. No lab axis
convention is assumed, because the repository holds two conflicting ones.

## Synthetic Fixture

All fixture values are invented. Nothing is transcribed from a SimTK model.
The fixture is generated by ElementTree string building in
`fixture_model.py` and `fixture_coupling.py` (OpenSim `spine`), so no OpenSim
import is needed to write it.

Topology, caudal to cranial:

- `ground` → `pelvis` (FreeJoint) → `sacrum` (WeldJoint) → one CustomJoint
  `<LEVEL>_jnt` per level → `thorax_proxy` (WeldJoint).
- The default levels are the five lumbar levels L5-S1 to L1-L2.
- Each level has rotation axes Z, X, Y with coordinates `<level>_flex_ext`,
  `<level>_lat_bend` and `<level>_axial_rot`, and constant-zero translations.
- Coordinate ranges are ±1 rad.
- The neutral offset is $T_{i,0} = [R_z(\lambda_i) \mid (0, L_{\mathrm{inf}}, 0)]$
  on the parent offset frame. The child frame is the identity.

Invented parameters:

| Parameter | Value (Invented) |
|---|---|
| Lordosis $\lambda_i$, L5-S1 to L1-L2 | 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 deg |
| Sacral slope (base weld) | 30 deg |
| Thorax tilt (terminal weld) | 5 deg |
| Pelvis | 10 kg, 0.10 m |
| Sacrum | 1.5 kg, 0.05 m |
| Each vertebra | 1 kg, 0.04 m |
| Thorax proxy | 20 kg |
| Inertia | Uniform cylinder, radius 0.05 m along Y |

Fixture variants:

- **Coupled fixture.** The law's independent coordinates sit on a massless
  driver body, `spine_coupling_driver`, attached to the pelvis. One
  `CoordinateCouplerConstraint` per level axis prescribes
  $q_{\mathrm{dep}} = \sum_k C_{i,r,k}\,\phi_k$. Only linear laws are
  representable. The mass matrix is singular, so the coupled fixture is
  kinematic only.
- **Muscled fixture.** Eight bilateral `Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle` objects
  run `pelvis` → `L3` (via point) → `thorax_proxy`:
  - erector spinae, rectus abdominis, external oblique and internal oblique;
  - maximum isometric forces 1500, 900, 700 and 600 N;
  - optimal fibre length 0.12 m and zero pennation;
  - tendon slack length = neutral path length minus optimal fibre length.
- **One-level fixture.** Level L3-L4 only. Eight muscles act on three degrees
  of freedom, so the inverse-dynamics moments are reachable with redundancy
  five. The static-optimization acceptance tests use it.
- **Five-level muscled fixture.** Eight lumped muscles cannot span 15 level
  degrees of freedom. Reserves are therefore needed, and every frame is
  flagged (measured reserve share 0.38 to 0.46).

The fixture geometry is not anatomical. Passing its tests establishes
software correctness only.

## Composition

For a chain from the pelvis to a named terminal body (`T1` for Bruno,
`thorax_proxy` for the fixture, `torso` for `golf_humanoid`):
$$T_{\mathrm{pelvis}\to\mathrm{terminal}} = T_{\mathrm{base}}\,
T_{1}\, T_{2} \cdots T_{n}\, T_{\mathrm{term}},$$
caudal factor first. $T_{\mathrm{base}}$ is the first chain body (for example
the sacrum) in the pelvis frame. $T_{\mathrm{term}}$ is the terminal body in
the last superior vertebra frame.

Per-level Cardan angles never add. The ADR-0055 worked example is a
regression test. Three levels with $(\theta_{FE}, \theta_{LB}, \theta_{AR})$
of $(-10, 5, -15)$, $(-10, 8, -20)$ and $(-15, 10, -25)$ degrees sum to
$(-35, 23, -60)$ but compose to $(-25.36, 31.83, -57.57)$ degrees. The angle
sum is available only as the labelled `angle_sum_diagnostic`.

The terminal body is not automatically the ISB thorax:

- ADR-0055 item 2 requires a separate, model-specific calibration
  $T_{\mathrm{terminal}\to\mathrm{thorax}}$ (thorax landmarks IJ, C7, PX, T8),
  and says it is never assumed to be the identity.
- No code path in this pathway estimates that calibration. The drive's
  alignment $A$ (see Kinematic Input and Drive) defaults to the identity.

Software verification:

- Composition holds to $10^{-9}$ in the analytic tests.
- The native fixture pose (thorax proxy and every intermediate vertebra in
  the pelvis frame, random level angles within ±0.4 rad) equals
  `SegmentalPose.compose()` to $10^{-9}$.
- A reversed composition order differs by more than $10^{-3}$ (negative
  control).

## Coupling Laws and Sign Maps

A coupling law maps independent coordinates $\phi \in \mathbb{R}^{n_\phi}$ to
per-level ISB angles $\theta_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ (rad). It prescribes
kinematics only. For inverse dynamics, static optimization and joint
reactions, every constraint of the model copy, couplers included, has
`isEnforced = False`, so constraint multipliers never enter a load.

Law families (`coupling.py`, shared `spine`):

| Family | Equation | Jacobian |
|---|---|---|
| Linear | $\theta_i = C_i\,\phi$, $C_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times n_\phi}$, cross-axis terms allowed | $C_i$ |
| State-dependent | $\theta_i = C_i(s)\,\phi$, $C_i$ piecewise linear in $s = \phi_k$ over strictly increasing breakpoints, held constant outside them | $C_i(s) + (\mathrm{d}C_i/\mathrm{d}s\,\phi)\,e_k^{\mathsf T}$, right-hand slope at interior breakpoints, zero slope outside |
| Polynomial | $\theta_{i,a} = o + \sum_{k=0}^{4} c_k (\phi_d - x_0)^k$ for one driver $d$; unlisted axes are zero | Polynomial derivative in $\phi_d$ |

Every law carries an id, a version and a citation. The regional fraction of
axis $a$ over a level set $R$ is
$f_R(a) = \sum_{i \in R}\theta_{i,a} / \sum_{i}\theta_{i,a}$; it raises when
the total is below $10^{-12}$ in magnitude.

### Shipped Laws

The shipped laws are in `src/config/spine_coupling_laws.json` and are built
by `coupling_data.py` (shared `spine`):

| Law | Construction | Source Status |
|---|---|---|
| `bruno2015_regional` | Diagonal $C_i = \mathrm{diag}(p_a / (100\, n_r))$ with regional shares $p$ lumbar/thoracic 51/49 (flexion), 27/73 (lateral bending), 17/83 (axial rotation), $n_L = 5$, $n_T = 12$. The uniform spread within a region is an assumption | Bruno 2015 Table B1: `verified_from_primary: true` (main text only, PMC5101035); PDF re-check recommended |
| `fujii2007_lumbar` | One coordinate, trunk axial rotation. $C_i = \mathrm{sign} \odot \bar\theta_i / 45°$, a 3 × 1 column per level T12-L1 to L5-S1 from the mean segment angles at 45 deg of trunk rotation. Linearity in rotation is an assumption. Gains do not sum to 1 | Fujii 2007 Table F1 (n = 10): `verified_from_primary: true` (PMC2223353 full text, two agreeing extractions); PDF re-check, author list and DOI pending (#12737) |
| `uniform_reference` | $C_i = I/17$ | Repository reference, not literature |

The per-level laws `bruno2015_per_level` (Bruno Supplemental Table 2) and
`pearcy1984_lumbar` are recorded as `pending` with no numbers and refuse to
build (#12743).

Sign map for `fujii2007_lumbar`:

- Fujii reports coupled flexion positive as flexion, and coupled lateral
  bending relative to the direction of trunk rotation.
- The JSON field `distribution.isb_sign` maps these to ISB signs: flexion
  $-1$, lateral bending $-1$, axial rotation $+1$.
- For a positive (left) axial rotation, flexion is ISB-negative and a
  same-direction (left) bend is ISB-negative.

### Fujii Parity Defect

`fujii2007_lumbar` is linear in one coordinate, so every coupled term is odd
in the trunk rotation $\phi$.

- **Coupled flexion.** Fujii measured flexion for rotation to either side, so
  this term is even in $\phi$. The shipped law turns it into coupled
  extension for a negative (right) rotation. For a right-handed backswing the
  law therefore has the wrong flexion sign.
- **Coupled lateral bend.** Fujii reports it relative to the rotation
  direction, so it is correctly odd.

This is a declared defect of the linear single-coordinate form, not of the
transcription. No test covers right rotation. A fix needs an even/odd law
form, which is a code change and is listed under Limitations.

### Coupler Extraction and Restriction

- `coupler_extraction.extract_coupling_law` (OpenSim `spine`) reads an OpenSim
  model's couplers back into a law. Linear and low-order polynomial couplers
  are exact. Spline and piecewise-linear couplers become a state-dependent
  law that is exact at the knots only. Unsupported function types raise.
- `coupling.restrict_to_levels` (shared `spine`) restricts a law to a model's
  level range. It keeps $C_i$ bit-identical, tags the version
  `<version>+levels:<first>..<last>` and marks the citation as a repository
  operation. Per-level ratios are kept. Absolute shares are not, because the
  distribution solve rescales $\phi$. A law covering fewer levels than the
  model fails the drive stage.

## Distribution and Residual

Distributing a pelvis-to-terminal rotation over levels is underdetermined. It
is defined through a fixed law (`distribution.py`, shared `spine`):
$$\phi^{*} = \arg\min_{\ell \le \phi \le u} \left\lVert r(\phi) \right\rVert_2,
\qquad r(\phi) = \log\!\left(R_{\mathrm{target}}^{\mathsf T}\, R(\phi)\right)^{\vee},
\qquad R(\phi) = B \Bigl[\prod_{i=1}^{n} N_i R_{ZXY}(\theta_i(\phi))\Bigr] E.$$

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $R_{\mathrm{target}}$ | Target terminal-body rotation in the pelvis frame |
| $\log(\cdot)^{\vee}$ | SO(3) logarithm as a rotation vector (rad); its norm is the geodesic residual |
| $B$ | Base rotation: first inferior body in the pelvis frame (`ChainOffsets`, identity when omitted) |
| $N_i$ | Neutral rotation block of $T_{i,0}$ |
| $E$ | Terminal rotation: terminal body in the last superior vertebra frame (`ChainOffsets`, identity when omitted) |
| $\ell, u$ | Bounds on the independent coordinates; default unbounded ($\pm\infty$). They do not enforce model coordinate ranges |
| Product order | Caudal level first |

Rules:

- The law is never altered to close the residual. The geodesic residual
  (rad) and the convergence flag are outputs. An unreachable target is
  flagged, never repaired.
- The residual is recomputed independently from the solved pose. It agrees
  with the solver's value to $10^{-10}$.
- Every per-level output carries `distribution_source`, for example
  `coupling:<law_id>@<version>`, `ik:<...>`, `measured:<...>` or
  `movement_variant:<...>`.

### Numerical Method

The solver is `scipy.optimize.least_squares` with `method="trf"`.

- Defaults: `tol_rad` $= 10^{-8}$ and `max_iter` $= 200$, passed as
  `max_nfev`.
- Stopping tolerances: `ftol` = `xtol` = `gtol` =
  $\max(10^{-5}\,\mathrm{tol\_rad}, 10^{-15})$.
- Start point: zeros, clipped to the bounds. A series is warm-started from the
  previous frame's solution, so each frame returns one local minimiser.
- `converged` is `status > 0` of the solver.

The Jacobian is analytic:
$$\frac{\partial r}{\partial \phi} = J_r^{-1}(r)\, W, \qquad
W = \sum_{i,k} (R_i S_i)^{\mathsf T} a_{ik}
\left(\frac{\partial \theta_i}{\partial \phi}\right)_{k,:},$$
$$J_r^{-1}(r) = I + \tfrac12 [r]_\times + c(\vartheta)\,[r]_\times^2, \qquad
c(\vartheta) = \frac{1}{\vartheta^2} - \frac{1 + \cos\vartheta}{2\vartheta\sin\vartheta}.$$

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $R_i$ | $R_{ZXY}(\theta_i)$ of level $i$ |
| $S_i$ | Suffix rotation $\bigl(\prod_{j > i} N_j R_j\bigr) E$ |
| $a_{ik}$ | Axis of angle $k$ of level $i$ in its parent frame: $e_z$, $R_z e_x$, $R_z R_x e_y$ |
| $W$ | $3 \times n_\phi$ body-frame Jacobian |
| $\vartheta$ | $\lVert r \rVert$; for $\vartheta < 10^{-4}$, $c = 1/12 + \vartheta^2/720$ |

The analytic Jacobian matches finite differences to $10^{-7}$.

### Observability

An SVD of $W$ gives the observability report:

- **Rank.** The rank counts singular values
  $\sigma > \max(10^{-8}\sigma_{\max}, 10^{-12})$.
- **Underdetermined flag.** The law is flagged `underdetermined` when
  rank $< n_\phi$. This covers laws with more than three coordinates, and
  also laws with dependent columns and $n_\phi \le 3$.
- **Flagged coordinates.** The report lists the null space, and
  `flagged_coordinates` names every coordinate whose null-space row norm
  exceeds $10^{-6}$.
- **Unobservable directions.** The left null space is reported as
  `unobservable_target_directions`.

## Kinematic Input and Drive

### Golf Humanoid Input

`read_golf_humanoid_motion(motion_path, model_path)` (`golf_input.py`,
OpenSim `spine`) does the following:

- reads a `golf_humanoid` `.sto` or `.mot` table and converts `inDegrees=yes`
  tables to radians;
- reads events from `event_<name>` header lines;
- evaluates the trunk rotation natively from the `back` CustomJoint
  (coordinates `lumbar_extension` $e$, `lumbar_bending` $b$ and
  `lumbar_rotation` $r$ about Z, X and Y):
  $$R_{\mathrm{pelvis}\to\mathrm{torso}} = R_{po}\, R_z(e)\, R_x(b)\, R_y(r)\, R_{to}^{\mathsf T},$$
  where $R_{po}$ and $R_{to}$ are the joint's pelvis and torso offset-frame
  rotations.

`resample` interpolates rotations by Slerp.

### Segmental Drive and Calibration

`drive_segmental_model` (`drive.py`, OpenSim `spine`) distributes the trunk
rotation frame by frame.

Chain offsets:

- `chain_offsets_from_model` reads $B$ and $E$ natively at zero coordinates.
- The pelvis-to-first-body and last-vertebra-to-terminal connections are
  assumed rigid.
- The level map must be verified; otherwise the drive raises `ValueError`.

Target and alignment:

- The target is $R_\star = R_{\mathrm{pelvis}\to\mathrm{torso}}\, A$.
- $A$ (`DriveOptions.torso_alignment`) is the segmental terminal frame
  expressed in the `golf_humanoid` torso frame. It defaults to the identity,
  and the pelvis body frames of the two models are assumed to coincide.
- These are unvalidated caller assumptions, not calibration evidence. A wrong
  $A$ biases every per-level angle without raising the geodesic residual.

Law and validity:

- Without a law id, the law is extracted from the model's own couplers. The
  law must cover exactly the model's levels.
- A frame is invalid when the solve did not converge or, if
  `tolerance_rad` is set, when the residual exceeds it.
- `DriveOptions.tolerance_rad` and `SpineStudyRequest.drive_tolerance_rad`
  default to `None`. With the default, convergence alone decides validity,
  and a converged but badly mismatched target stays valid. A study that
  claims endpoint reproduction must declare a finite tolerance.
- Invalid frames are kept as solved and never repaired.

Coordinate table and export:

- Level coordinates are $q = s\,\theta$, where $s = \pm 1$ is the level-map
  axis sign.
- The six pelvis coordinates are unwrapped intrinsic Euler angles of the
  pelvis pose in ground plus the pelvis origin:
  - `golf` encoding: sequence ZXY (`pelvis_tilt`, `pelvis_list`,
    `pelvis_rotation`, `pelvis_tx/ty/tz`);
  - `fixture` encoding: sequence XYZ (`pelvis_rx/ry/rz` for the free joint).
- The ground-pelvis offset frames are assumed to be identity.
- `export_mot` writes the table natively with `STOFileAdapter`, with
  `inDegrees=no` and a `distribution_source` header line.

### Motion Reader

`read_segmental_kinematics` (`read_kinematics.py`, OpenSim `spine`) inverts
the export.

- It recovers $\theta = s\,q$ and $T_i = T_{i,0}\,T(R_{ZXY}(\theta_i), 0)$
  into a `SegmentalKinematicsSeries`.
- A non-empty `distribution_source` is required, and it must match the header
  when the header has one.
- With `verify_native=True` the realised terminal rotation is checked against
  $B \cdot \mathrm{compose} \cdot E$ to $10^{-9}$.

Software verification:

- A synthetic input generated from the fixture's own law is recovered with a
  residual below $10^{-8}$ rad.
- The exported `.mot` replayed natively on the coupled fixture matches the
  target to $10^{-8}$.
- A law that cannot reach the target reports residuals above $10^{-3}$ rad and
  is flagged invalid under a $10^{-6}$ rad tolerance.
- A 654-frame `golf_humanoid` swing driving a 17-level fixture with
  `bruno2015_regional` gave a maximum residual of $1.2 \times 10^{-13}$ rad
  (SPN-9b). This shows reachability on the fixture chain, not a physiological
  distribution.

## Golf Terms

Golf-instruction quantities are versioned measurands in `golf_terms.py`
(shared `spine`). Legacy implementations keep their numeric meaning under
legacy ids; new ids are new measurands. The handedness factor is $s = -1$ for
a right-handed and $s = +1$ for a left-handed golfer. The three JCS terms use
the `isb_spine` decomposition of the pelvis-to-thorax rotation.

| Term | Required Inputs | Definition | Units and Sign |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x_factor_jcs_axial` | `pelvis_to_thorax_rotation` | $s\,\theta_{AR}$ | deg, backswing positive |
| `trunk_lateral_flexion_jcs` | `pelvis_to_thorax_rotation` | $s\,\theta_{LB}$ | deg, lead side positive |
| `trunk_extension_jcs` | `pelvis_to_thorax_rotation` | $\theta_{FE}$ | deg, extension positive, not handed |
| `x_factor_line_turn` | `points`, `t`, `events`, `up` (optional `point_pairs`) | Upper-trunk line turn minus pelvis line turn about `up`; points are rotated so `up` maps to +Z | deg, positive for a right-handed backswing, negated for left-handed |
| `x_factor_position_proxy` | `joint_positions`, `shoulder_joint_idx`, `hip_joint_idx` | deg(shoulder) − deg(hip) of radian joint coordinates | deg, legacy, not handed |
| `x_factor_euler_yaw_legacy_v1` | `thorax_euler`, `pelvis_euler` (rad, third column is yaw) | deg(thorax yaw − pelvis yaw) | deg, legacy |
| `side_bend_tilt` | `trunk_axis`, `up`, `target` | Trunk-axis tilt from `up`, returned as [total, toward_target, lateral]; lateral axis = forward × up | deg |
| `crunch_factor_legacy_v1` | `lateral_bend_rad`, `axial_rotation_rad` | $\lvert\mathrm{deg}(\mathrm{lat})\rvert\,\lvert\mathrm{deg}(\mathrm{rot})\rvert/100$ | deg²/100, legacy |
| `crunch_factor_rate` | `trunk_lateral_flexion_jcs`, `x_factor_jcs_axial`, `time_s` | $l(t)\,\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t$ | deg·deg/s |
| `early_extension` | `pelvis_position`, `target`, `up`, `events`, `ball_position` | $d(t_{\mathrm{address}}) - d(t)$, $d$ the horizontal distance of the pelvis to the target line through the ball | m, toward the ball positive |
| `reverse_spine_angle` | `trunk_axis`, `up`, `target`, `events` | `toward_target` tilt of `side_bend_tilt` at the top event | deg |

Notes:

- **JCS terms at gimbal lock.** At $|\theta_{LB}| = 90°$ the JCS terms return
  NaN for FE and AR.
- **Crunch-factor rate.** In `crunch_factor_rate`,
  $l = s\,\theta_{LB}$ and $x = s\,\theta_{AR}$ are both handed golf terms in
  degrees. The derivative is `numpy.gradient(x, time_s)`, which needs at
  least two strictly increasing samples. No further handedness, smoothing or
  unwrapping is applied. The term is attributed to Sugaya, Tsuchiya and
  Moriya (1999) via Cole and Grimshaw (2014); the primary definition is
  unverified (`verified_from_primary: false`, #12737).

### Segmental Contributions

Segmental contributions are path dependent and are not Cardan angles. For a
JCS term $f$ the contribution of level $i$ is
$$c_i = f\!\left(\textstyle\prod_{j \le i} T_j\right) -
f\!\left(\textstyle\prod_{j < i} T_j\right), \qquad f(\text{empty}) = 0,$$
with caudal-first truncation. The prefixes are `pose.relative_rotation`
products and include each level's neutral offset, the first level's included.
`segmental_contributions` attributes the supplied `SegmentalPose` chain only
($B = E = A = I$).

`segmental_contribution_breakdown` (#12822) attributes the rest of the
pelvis-to-thorax path. The global term is $f(B\,C\,E\,A)$ with
$C=\prod_i T_i$, $B$ the base rotation (pelvis to first body), $E$ the
terminal rotation (last vertebra to terminal body) and $A$ the drive
alignment. With $P_0=B$, $P_k=B\prod_{j\le k}T_j$, $P_E=P_nE$ and
$P_A=P_EA$, it returns $c_\mathrm{base}=f(B)$, $c_k=f(P_k)-f(P_{k-1})$,
$c_\mathrm{terminal}=f(P_E)-f(P_n)$ and $c_\mathrm{alignment}=f(P_A)-f(P_E)$.
Only the supplied rotations are reported, as named non-level entries that are
never folded into a level. The sum telescopes to $f(P_A)$, and a
postcondition checks closure to $10^{-9}$ degrees on finite samples;
gimbal-locked prefixes give NaN.

`contribution_remainder`, with the same optional rotations, checks internal
telescoping only. It does not verify closure to a separately evaluated
pelvis-to-thorax term, so callers must pass the same $B$, $E$ and $A$ they
used for the global term. A contribution depends on $B$ and on every level
caudal to it, and is not that level's own angle. `level_angle_stack`
attributes the supplied chain only.

Software verification: the analyzer, swing metrics and API X-factor paths
delegate to the registry under their legacy ids, golden-tested to
$10^{-12}$.
